title: LEBRE research record — v0.55
description:
Research record of LEBRE (Lifecycle-governed Evidence-Based Resource Evolution), an online one-step-ahead forecaster for time series with inputs, at a counted cost per step. Its structural core accepts each structural change (adding, removing, swapping or refining the response to a whole input) by an anytime-valid sequential test (e-process) of predictive improvement, within an online multiple-testing procedure. Layer M1 adds a precision expert combined with the core by AdaHedge; layer M2 starts the forecast from a declared trivial reference (zero, persistence or seasonal naive) and combines two paths by an (A,B)-Prod.

Version v0.55 changes the question the evidence answers: an external input is accepted only if it improves the core forecast, which already contains the memory of the target, while the target's own past and the residual state are tested against the level structure; an innovation structure, with the same accepted units, carries their information to the forecast when the target is integrated; a soft gate in screening only gives a test slot to an internal unit that explains what the core still gets wrong; and the test scale becomes predictable and measured on the scale of one step. It was promoted on 2026-10-17 by a pre-registered binding rule in a single run on a new reserve of 84 series (basins, buildings, wind and solar plants, ECB euro reference rates): no family worse than v0.54 beyond the margin (ratio 0.993 to 1.008); placebo random-walk inputs in the final structure on 0 of 84 series, against 4 for v0.54; median per-series cost 0.989 of v0.54's. A comparison with 12 external models (reference only) is included. A formal note argues that the e-processes are valid under any predictable learner (single author, not independently reviewed), with erratum 01.

This archive contains the Python reference implementations, a C99 port of the core with firmware and scripts for a simulated Cortex-M4F microcontroller (Renode), experiment scripts, pre-registrations, result tables, reports, frozen versions with SHA-256 manifests (v0.1, v0.51, v0.52, v0.53, v0.54, v0.55), the self-contained v0.55 specification (English and Portuguese) and scripts to verify integrity and reproduce results. Development and validations are in the public LEBRE Lab (https://github.com/Iquitim/lebre-lab). Raw third-party data, per-series prediction arrays and toolchains are not included; they are listed with SHA-256 in docs/research/ARTIFACTS_MANIFEST.tsv.

Scope and limits. One-step forecasting; on basins, a small significant loss against v0.54 (1.008) and a recursive-least-squares ARX of the same cost class is better; the gain on integrated series was shown on synthetic data only; weak real relations are registered as structure more slowly; structural false-change control remains empirical (joint theoretical bound 2 alpha); no formal error guarantee in the original scale for M1 and M2; microcontroller costs only for the core and from a simulator; no component is original. See the specification, section 22.
